files.why: The cloud never supplies LAN IPs, so setup skips every device with no stored address and creates no coordinator, so there are no entities. This is passive DHCP-only IP discovery. Discovery relies solely on the registered_devices DHCP matcher, which only fires for DHCP traffic seen after the devices are registered. A fix probably needs a MAC-prefix DHCP matcher or another discovery mechanism.

The coordinator only polls once and then relies on the websocket subscription. subscribe() retries only on TraccarException. If the connection closes cleanly (client.subscribe returns normally) it never resubscribes, and a ConfigEntryAuthFailed raised in the background task is not handled. Updates therefore stop silently until the entry is reloaded. The fix is to loop and resubscribe after any disconnect, or restore a fallback polling interval.
The subscription runs as a one-shot background task with no supervision. A failure or clean return there is never restarted or reported to the config entry.

get_device_endpoint resolves the Thermostat endpoint to its compose parent, which on the Aqara M3 hub is the root endpoint 0, so the AC and the bridge share one device ID; it should never return the root/bridge endpoint as a compose parent for a bridged endpoint.
It builds the device registry entry from get_device_endpoint, so the AC gets merged into the bridge entry, and the via_device check is skipped or points at itself (the 'Connected via' loop).
The entity's DeviceInfo identifiers come from get_device_id, so they must match the corrected separate bridge and AC devices.

files.lines: calc_derivative(), the total_increasing negative-derivative drop branch (~lines 540-553)
files.why: When the source returns from unavailable with a reset value of 0, the old value is taken from `_last_valid_state_time` (the pre-midnight total) and the negative delta is dropped with a bare `return`. That return neither updates `_last_valid_state_time` to the new 0 baseline nor calls `async_write_ha_state()`/`_write_native_value()`, so `_attr_available = True` is never published and the sensor stays Unavailable until a second changed sample arrives. The fix is to reset the baseline to the new state and timestamp and write a state (a derivative of 0 or None) in that branch.

The radon sensor uses a bare "Bq/m³" string with no device_class, so unit conversion to pCi/L is unavailable; it should set device_class=SensorDeviceClass.RADON and native_unit_of_measurement=UnitOfRadiationConcentration.BECQUEREL_PER_CUBIC_METER.
Once the sensor uses the RADON device class, the translation_key and its custom icon entry are redundant and can be removed, because the device class supplies the icon.

files.why: is_on only matches state_status == on_value exactly, so when the appliance reports combined supercooling_superfreezing (146) or another status the switch stays off, and there's no optimistic state update after send_action.

Setup forces an update-before-add and the entity state/timeline is computed against the full calendar, so a large calendar blocks the event loop for about 90 seconds; drop update_before_add and keep the timeline work in the executor with a bounded lookahead.
Parsing the large ICS (with the compat-mode rewrite) is the expensive step and must stay off the event loop, with a bounded cost for large calendars.
Large downloaded text and parsing happen here on each refresh, so this is where heavy work must stay in the executor.

The 91s "Updating state" warning comes from entity setup with update_before_add=True. The timeline walk and the initial state computation for a large calendar should run only in the executor-backed _async_update_timeline, never inline in the event loop.
res.text decodes the whole large response synchronously on the event loop (charset detection can be slow), and the parse is not bounded. Decoding and parsing should both be moved off the loop.
The heavy parse of a big Outlook calendar runs through the compat mode and IcsCalendarStream, so any decoding or timeline preparation that still touches the loop belongs in this executor job.
The config flow also reads res.text on the loop and parses the whole large calendar just to validate it, which is the "loading for a while" part of the report.

is_on only compares device.state_status to a single on_value (supercooling=14 / superfreezing=13), so it stays off whenever the device reports a different status (e.g. combined supercooling_superfreezing=146, or the status no longer changes), and the switch also never writes optimistic state after sending the action.
The status enum mapping for supercooling/superfreezing/combined (13, 14, 146) is what the switch state is derived from and may need adjusting so the combined state counts as on.

files.lines: MieleSuperSwitch.is_on (~lines 223-230) and the supercooling/superfreezing SWITCH_TYPES entries (lines 53-79)
files.why: is_on only checks state_status == supercooling/superfreezing, so it stays off when the device reports the combined supercooling_superfreezing (146) or another status. The fix is to derive on/off correctly, for example by also treating status 146 as on for both switches.
The status values used for the on-state comparison may be incomplete or mismatched (supercooling_superfreezing=146 and the missing_to_none behaviour), so the state mapping may need adjusting.
